newsitem.title: GERMANY: Police detain several people in German kidnap case.
newsitem.headline: Police detain several people in German kidnap case.

text.p: Police probing the kidnapping of German multi-millionaire Jakub Fiszmann searched several buildings and apartments in Frankfurt, Mainz and Wiesbaden, and detained several people, prosecutors said on Wednesday
A spokesman for the prosecutors declined to say what they may have found or how many people had been detained, adding that more details would be given at an afternoon news conference.
Fiszmann, 40, has been missing since his abduction on October 1.
Police said the findings from the search were still being evaluated. No more information would be released until all the information had been analysed, they added.
Fiszmann's brother, Georg, paid a 4 million mark ($2.6 million) ransom on October 10 for his release, but his kidnappers failed to free him as promised the following day.
On Tuesday authorities said they believed that Fiszmann was still alive, following a statement from the kidnappers that the businessman had enough provisions to survive for four weeks.
Earlier this week, 25 police officers searched a former U.S. army arms depot near Frankfurt for clues.
The Fiszmann family, one of the richest in Germany, this week offered a one million mark ($650,000) reward for information about the whereabouts of the missing businessman.
Police in Wiesbaden said they hoped the offer would lead to clues to help free Fiszmann.

Based on their investigations so far, the police said they thought the kidnappers were German. There had been speculation in the media that Fiszmann had been kidnapped by the Russian mafia or a terrorist organisation.

The last confirmation that Fiszmann was alive came on October 2, one day after his abduction during which he was injured in a scuffle, when he spoke with a contact believed to be his girlfriend. ($1=1.5374 Mark)
